chapterNote: The psalm of the friend who turned. It opens in pure panic — a heart writhing, death's terrors falling, fear and trembling, horror pulling itself over him like a blanket — and produces the most human wish in the Psalter: oh, for wings like a dove, to fly away and settle down, to lodge far off in the wilderness and outrun this storm. But the storm is a city, and inside it violence and strife patrol the walls day and night while ruin, oppression and fraud keep the streets. Then the real wound: it was not an enemy who taunted him, or he could have carried it; not a hater who rose against him, or he could have hidden. It was you — a man my own size, my companion, my familiar friend, with whom I used to sweeten counsel and walk in the house of God in the crowd. His words were smoother than butter and softer than oil, and they were drawn swords. David's answer is a routine: evening and morning and noon I will complain, and He will hear my voice — and one line the church has carried ever since: cast what He has given you on the LORD, and He will hold you up. The psalm never says the friendship was repaired. It says the trust was placed somewhere it could not be broken.

1.text: Turn Your ear to my prayer, O God, and do not hide away from the grace I am begging for.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach] on Neginoth [neginah — stringed music], Maschil [maskil], A Psalm of David. Give ear [azan] to my prayer [tephillah], O God [Elohim]; and hide [alam] not Yourself from my supplication [techinnah — plea for grace].
1.notes: haazinah Elohim tephillati (H238, H430, H8605): give EAR, God, to my prayer — ve-al-titallam mi-techinnati (H5956, H8467): and do not HIDE YOURSELF from my techinnah, my grace-plea. The verb is the one used of a man who looks away from his brother's lost ox (Deuteronomy 22:1-4): do not pretend You did not see. Neginoth (H5058): stringed accompaniment.

2.text: Pay attention to me; answer me. I cannot keep still in my complaining, and I moan aloud,
2.amp: Attend [qashab] unto me, and hear [anah — answer] me: I mourn [rud — am restless] in my complaint [siach], and make a noise;
2.notes: haqshibah li va-aneni (H7181, H6030): pay attention to me and ANSWER me; arid be-sichi ve-ahimah (H7300, H7879, H1949): I roam restlessly in my siach — the complaint-word of Psalm 102's title — and I moan. rud is the pacing of an animal that cannot settle; the psalm begins with a body that will not be still.

3.text: because of the voice of the enemy, because of the pressure of the wicked — for they topple trouble onto me and in anger they hound me.
3.amp: Because of the voice [qol] of the enemy [oyeb], because [panim] of the oppression of the wicked [rasha]: for they cast [mot] iniquity [aven] upon me, and in wrath [aph] they hate me.
3.notes: mi-qol oyeb mi-pene aqat rasha (H6963, H341, H6440, H7563): from the VOICE of the enemy, from the face of the wicked man's pressure. ki-yamitu alai aven (H4131, H205): for they TOPPLE wickedness onto me — mot, the verb for a thing sliding off a shelf. u-be-aph yistemuni (H639, H7852): and in anger they bear a grudge against me, the verb used of Esau toward Jacob (Genesis 27:41).

4.text: My heart writhes inside me, and the terrors of death have fallen on me.
4.amp: My heart [leb] is sore pained [chul — writhes] within [qereb] me: and the terrors [emah] of death [mavet] are fallen [naphal] upon me.
4.notes: libbi yachil be-qirbi (H3820, H2342, H7130): my heart WRITHES inside me — chul, the verb for a woman in labor (Isaiah 26:17); ve-emot mavet naphelu alai (H367, H4194, H5307): and death's terrors have FALLEN on me — emah, the dread that fell on Abram in the dark (Genesis 15:12). Not fear of an outcome; the thing itself has landed.

5.text: Fear and trembling come over me, and shuddering has covered me over.
5.amp: Fearfulness [yirah] and trembling [raad] are come [bo] upon me, and horror has overwhelmed ['covered', kasah, the KJV margin] me.
5.notes: yirah va-raad yabo bi (H3374, H7461, H935): fear and TREMBLING come into me — raad, the shaking of Psalm 48:6's kings; va-tekhassseni pallatsut (H3680, H6427): and shuddering has COVERED me, the margin's literal — pallatsut, a horror that comes over a man the way a garment does (Job 21:6; Ezekiel 7:18).

6.text: And I said: 'Oh, that I had wings like a dove! I would fly away and settle down.
6.amp: And I said [amar], Oh that [natan] I had wings [eber] like a dove [yonah]! for then would I fly away [uph], and be at rest [shakan — settle].
6.notes: va-omar mi-yitten-li eber ka-yonah (H559, H5414, H83, H3123): 'who will give me' — the Hebrew idiom of longing — a wing like a dove's; aphuah ve-eshkonah (H5774, H7931): I would FLY and SETTLE — shakan, the tabernacle-verb, to come to rest somewhere and stay. The most human wish in the Psalter, and the psalm records it without embarrassment and without granting it.

7.text: Look — I would wander far off; I would spend the night in the wilderness. Selah.
7.amp: Lo, then would I wander far off [rachaq], and remain [lun — lodge] in the wilderness [midbar]. Selah [Selah].
7.notes: hinneh archiq nedod (H7368, H5074): look — I would take my wandering FAR; alin ba-midbar (H3885, H4057): I would lodge in the wilderness — lun, to spend one night, the verb of Psalm 30:5's weeping. The wilderness is not romantic here; it is simply empty of people, which is the whole attraction. Selah.

8.text: I would hurry to my shelter, away from the driving wind, away from the storm.'
8.amp: I would hasten [chush] my escape from the windy [ruach] storm and tempest [saar].
8.notes: achishah miphlat li me-ruach soah mi-saar (H2363, H4655, H7307, H5584, H5591): I would HURRY my escape from the sweeping wind, from the saar, the whirlwind. The storm is a metaphor that the next verses identify: it is a city, and the weather in it is human speech (vv. 9-11, 21).

9.text: Confuse them, O Lord; divide their tongues — for I have seen violence and strife in the city.
9.amp: Destroy [bala], O Lord [Adonai], and divide their tongues [lashon]: for I have seen [raah] violence [chamas] and strife [rib] in the city [ir].
9.notes: balla Adonai palag leshonam (H1104, H136, H6385, H3956): swallow them up, Lord — DIVIDE their tongue: palag, the verb behind Peleg's name, 'for in his days the earth was divided' (Genesis 10:25), and the prayer is plainly for a second Babel (Genesis 11:7-9). ki-raiti chamas ve-rib ba-ir (H7200, H2555, H7379, H5892): for I have SEEN violence and strife in the city. Conspiracy runs on agreement; he asks God to break the agreement.

10.text: Day and night they patrol her walls, and trouble and grief are inside her.
10.amp: Day [yomam] and night [layil] they go about [sabab] it upon the walls [chomah] thereof: mischief [aven] also and sorrow [amal] are in the midst [qereb] of it.
10.notes: yomam va-lailah yesobbeha al-chomoteha (H3119, H3915, H5437, H2346): day and night they CIRCLE her on her walls — the posture of a watchman turned into the posture of a predator; ve-aven ve-amal be-qirbah (H205, H5999): and wickedness and trouble are inside her. The guard on the wall is the danger within it.

11.text: Ruin is inside her; oppression and fraud never leave her public square.
11.amp: Wickedness [havvah — ruin] is in the midst [qereb] thereof: deceit and guile [mirmah] depart [mush] not from her streets.
11.notes: havvot be-qirbah (H1942, H7130): ruinous things are inside her; ve-lo-yamish me-rechobah tokh u-mirmah (H4185, H7339, H8496, H4820): and from her rechob — the broad place, the public square where justice was done — oppression and deceit do not DEPART. The one open space in an ancient city, the courtroom of the town, permanently occupied by fraud.

12.text: For it is not an enemy who taunts me — I could carry that; it is not one who hates me who has risen against me — I could hide from him.
12.amp: For it was not an enemy [oyeb] that reproached [charaph — taunted] me; then I could have borne [nasa] it: neither was it he that hated [sane] me that did magnify [gadal] himself against me; then I would have hid [satar] myself from him:
12.notes: ki lo-oyeb yecharpheni ve-essa (H341, H2778, H5375): for it is not an enemy taunting me — then I would CARRY it, nasa, the bearing-verb; lo-mesani alai higdil ve-essater mimmennu (H8130, H1431, H5641): not one hating me who magnified himself over me — then I would hide from him. Two ordinary griefs he knows how to survive, named in order to say that this is not one of them.

13.text: But it is you — a man my own size, my companion, my familiar friend.
13.amp: But it was you, a man [enosh] mine equal ['according to my rank', erek, the KJV margin], my guide [alluph — companion], and mine acquaintance [yada].
13.notes: ve-attah enosh ke-erki (H582, H6187): but YOU — a man 'according to my rank', the margin's literal: my own valuation, my equal; alluphi u-meyuddai (H441, H3045): my alluph — an intimate, the word also used for a tribal chief and for a tamed animal — and my known one. Ahithophel, David's counselor, went over to Absalom (2 Samuel 15:31); the psalm does not name him, which is why it has fit so many.

14.text: We used to sweeten counsel together; we walked into the house of God with the crowd.
14.amp: We took sweet ['Who sweetened counsel', sod, the KJV margin] counsel [sod — intimate circle] together [yachad], and walked [halak] unto the house [bayith] of God [Elohim] in company.
14.notes: asher yachdav namtiq sod (H3162, H4985, H5475): together we would make SOD sweet — sod is the private council, the inner circle of Psalm 25:14; be-bet Elohim nehallekh be-ragesh (H1004, H430, H1980, H7285): in the house of God we walked in the throng. The betrayal is doubled by the setting: they went to church together.

15.text: Let death come on them by surprise; let them go down alive into Sheol — for evil is at home among them.
15.amp: Let death [mavet] seize upon them, and let them go down [yarad] quick [chay — alive] into hell ['the grave', sheol, the KJV margin]: for wickedness [ra] is in their dwellings, and among [qereb] them.
15.notes: yashi mavet alemo (H5377, H4194): let death come on them by SURPRISE — the verb for being deceived, death arriving as an ambush. yeredu sheol chayyim (H3381, H7585, H2416): let them go down to Sheol ALIVE — Korah, Dathan and Abiram, whom the ground swallowed breathing (Numbers 16:30-33). ki-raot bi-megaram be-qirbam (H7451, H4033, H7130): for evils are in their lodging, inside them. The psalm's one imprecation, and its model is a judgment God actually performed.

16.text: As for me, I call out to God, and the LORD saves me.
16.amp: As for me, I will call [qara] upon God [Elohim]; and the LORD [YHWH] shall save [yasha] me.
16.notes: ani el-Elohim eqra (H430, H7121): as for ME — the pronoun that turns the psalm — to God I call; va-YHWH yoshieni (H3068, H3467): and the LORD will save me. Against the conspirators' circling (v. 10) and the friend's smoothness (v. 21), one line of ordinary practice.

17.text: Evening and morning and noon I complain and moan, and He hears my voice.
17.amp: Evening [ereb], and morning [boqer], and at noon, will I pray [siach — complain], and cry aloud [hamah]: and He shall hear [shama] my voice [qol].
17.notes: ereb va-boqer ve-tsohorayim asichah ve-ehemeh (H6153, H1242, H6672, H7878, H1993): evening and morning and noon I will COMPLAIN and moan — siach and hamah, the same two verbs as verse 2, now on a schedule; va-yishma qoli (H8085, H6963): and He hears my voice. Three fixed hours of prayer, the pattern Daniel kept in Babylon (Daniel 6:10): panic given a timetable.

18.text: He has ransomed my soul in peace from the battle against me, for there were many against me.
18.amp: He has delivered [padah — ransomed] my soul [nephesh] in peace [shalom] from the battle [qerab] that was against me: for there were many [rab] with me.
18.notes: padah be-shalom naphshi mi-qerab-li (H6299, H7965, H5315, H7128): He has RANSOMED my soul in shalom out of the battle that was at me. ki-be-rabbim hayu immadi (H7227): for they were many against me — or, as the KJV takes it, many were with me: the Hebrew allows either, and Elisha's servant at Dothan (2 Kings 6:16) is the reason the second reading has always been loved.

19.text: God hears and humbles them — He who sits enthroned from of old. Selah. Because they never change, they do not fear God.
19.amp: God [El] shall hear [shama], and afflict [anah] them, even He that abides [yashab — sits enthroned] of old [qedem]. Selah [Selah]. Because ['With whom also there be no changes, yet they', chaliphah, the KJV margin] they have no changes, therefore they fear [yare] not God [Elohim].
19.notes: yishma El ve-yaanem ve-yoshev qedem (H410, H8085, H6030, H3427, H6924): God hears and humbles them — He who SITS from of old, the throne of Psalm 9:7. asher en chaliphot lamo ve-lo yareu Elohim (H2487, H3372, H430): 'who have no changes' — chaliphot, changes of clothes, reliefs of a guard, turns of fortune: men whose lives have never been interrupted, and so they do not fear God. The psalm's diagnosis of comfortable irreligion (cf. Psalm 73:4-5).

20.text: He has put out his hands against those at peace with him; he has profaned his covenant.
20.amp: He has put forth [shalach] his hands [yad] against such as be at peace [shalom] with him: he has broken ['profaned', chalal, the KJV margin] his covenant [berith].
20.notes: shalach yadav bi-shlomav (H7971, H3027, H7965): he has stretched out his hands against those at PEACE with him — shalom, the same word as verse 18's peace, on the other side of the ledger; chillel berito (H2490, H1285): he has PROFANED his covenant, the margin's literal — chalal, the verb for desecrating the sanctuary. A broken friendship treated as sacrilege, because it was sworn.

21.text: His mouth was smoother than butter, but his heart was war; his words were softer than oil, and they were drawn swords.
21.amp: The words of his mouth [peh] were smoother [chalaq] than butter, but war [qerab] was in his heart [leb]: his words [dabar] were softer [rakak] than oil [shemen], yet were they drawn swords.
21.notes: chaleqe machmaot piv u-qerab libbo (H2505, H4260, H6310, H7128, H3820): smooth things of butter, his mouth — and his heart, war; rakku debarav mi-shemen ve-hemmah phetichot (H7401, H1697, H8081, H6609): his words were SOFTER than oil, and they were drawn blades — pethichot, things unsheathed. The verse the church quotes about flattery (cf. Proverbs 26:24-25); the smoothness is the weapon's polish.

22.text: Cast what He has given you on the LORD, and He Himself will hold you up; He will never let the righteous be shaken.
22.amp: Cast [shalak] your burden ['gift', yehab, the KJV margin] upon the LORD [YHWH], and He shall sustain [kul] you: He shall never [olam] suffer [natan] the righteous [tsaddiq] to be moved [mot].
22.notes: hashlekh al-YHWH yehabkha ve-hu yekhalkelekha (H7993, H3068, H3053, H3557): THROW on the LORD your yehab — a word used only here, from the verb 'to give': your lot, what has been handed you, which is why the margin offers 'gift' — and HE will sustain you, kul, the verb for keeping a household fed (Genesis 45:11). lo-yitten le-olam mot la-tsaddiq (H5414, H5769, H4131, H6662): He will never give the righteous over to tottering — mot, the toppling verb the enemies used in verse 3. 1 Peter 5:7 is this verse in Greek.

23.text: But You, O God, will bring them down to the pit of ruin; men of blood and deceit will not live out half their days — but I will trust in You.
23.amp: But You, O God [Elohim], shall bring them down [yarad] into the pit of destruction: bloody ['men of bloods and deceit', dam mirmah, the KJV margin] and deceitful [mirmah] men [enosh] shall not live out half ['shall not half their days', chatsah, the KJV margin] their days [yom]; but I will trust [batach] in You.
23.notes: ve-attah Elohim toridem li-ber shachat (H430, H3381, H875, H7845): but YOU, God, will bring them down to the well of the pit. anshe damim u-mirmah lo-yechetsu yemehem (H582, H1818, H4820, H2673, H3117): 'men of bloods and deceit', the margin's literal, will not HALVE their days — the life cut off at the midpoint, the opposite of Psalm 91:16's satisfaction with long life. va-ani ebtach-bakh (H982): but I — I will trust in You. The psalm ends where every honest one does: not with the friendship repaired but with the trust relocated.
